body:
<!-- pr-reviewer: 4aa5b1cc1410ac296f0369d72ad7b47777dd3a1d -->
**Independent review (v0.14.0 cut), static.** Verdict: **clean, no blocking items.**

I checked these:
- **No sign ever changes.** A `Band` texel has a nonzero composed value, and all of its 26 neighbours share its sign and are finite and nonzero; anything else is `Frozen`. Its magnitude starts at `cap` and only ever decreases (`next < u[i]`). Every neighbour magnitude it reads is at least 0: a frozen `|v|`, `cap`, or an earlier Godunov root. Godunov's root is at least `a1 + h/sqrt(3) > 0`. So the written magnitude is in `[h/sqrt(3), cap]`, and the sign comes from `phi`. Since `max(±mag, cut)` keeps the composed sign: for a negative composed value both layers were negative; for a positive one the new mesh is already positive.
- **The zero crossing never moves.** Frozen texels write back `phi` (f32 -> f64 -> f32 is exact), and `max(phi, cut) == phi` because `phi >= cut`. Any lattice cube with a `Band` corner has all eight corners inside that texel's 26-neighbourhood, all of one sign. A trilinear (or marching-tetrahedra) read of such a cube is a convex combination of same-sign values, so no zero can appear there. Any edge or cube that does carry a crossing has only frozen corners, and those are bit-identical.
- **Playback stays sign-correct.** `PackedBase::of` is called only from the play worker's `run()`, on `FieldPlay`'s frame-0 (uncut) stock. Later cut layers only grow. A backward scrub restores a checkpoint at or after frame 0, so the base's cut layer is never undercut by a frame.
- **It is bounded.** There is one classification pass (27 reads per texel) and exactly 8 ordered sweeps over band texels. There is no convergence loop, threads or hashing, so it is deterministic. A dims/len mismatch or a non-finite cell/cap is refused before anything is written, and the caller keeps the un-normalised lattice and logs to stderr.
- **Display only.** The only call site is the render pack. `march` and `deviate_field` still read the sparse field, and the CPU `preview()` is untouched.
- **Laws.** No unwrap/expect/panic in src. The new file is 230 lines and `stock_view.rs` is 292. Provenance is stated (Zhao 2005; Sussman-Smereka-Osher; Russo-Smereka). It sits in sim/app with no layering issue.

Notes, not blocking:
1. **Transient memory.** `phi` and `u` are `Vec<f64>`, plus a `Role` per texel, so about 17 B per texel over the packed lattice. At the 8M-texel pack limit that is about 136 MB extra, held on the play worker while `of` runs. `f32` would halve it with no loss, since the inputs and outputs are already `f32`.
2. The static `field_view` eye (`packed: None`) packs itself elsewhere and is not re-normalised. So the playback view and the static view shade slightly differently on the same stock. That is fine if intended, and worth a line in the PR or a follow-up.

Not approving or merging.

<!-- review-cost: estimated -->
**Estimated agent cost:** ~$1.14 (rough estimate from size: 488 changed lines)

No token usage was recorded for this PR, so this is calibrated from PRs with measured cost (our fix PRs, fix agent + review: median ~$1.20, ~$2.33 per 1,000 changed lines; floor $0.15, cap ~$3.60). For a contributor's PR it estimates what writing and reviewing it the way our agents work would cost, not what their session actually spent.

Blended upper estimate: 90 % input / 10 % output at list price (Opus 5.5 ~$5.60/M, Sonnet 5.5 ~$2.80/M, Haiku 5.5 ~$0.14/M). Cache reads make the real cost lower; main-session coordination isn't counted.
